answer: The cipher multiplier is published, charged in trellis, and lagoon lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4613 identities would post 807 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
